hottest.summary: Overview On November 9, 2026, N-able announced that it was responding to the public disclosure of critical vulnerabilities affecting N-central , its remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform. In a public disclosure titled Able2Shell, an independent researcher has published details and proof-of-concept (PoC) code covering 33 issues. According to the disclosure, the issues include unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE), privilege escalation to root, credential disclosure, and unauthorized account creation. One unauthenticated chain combines XML external entity (XXE) and session-handling weaknesses to execute code as the nable service account. Other demonstrated chains involve an administrator viewing malicious patch metadata or use ProductAdmin credentials. Rapid7 Intelligence is currently triaging the newly published details. Before the hotfix release on November 10, N-able reported scanning activity associated with the published PoC code and said it had no evidence that any customer environment had been successfully exploited. The vendor advised keeping N-central deployments offline while it developed and validated a hotfix. Hosted N-central classic environments were offline, according to the same notice. That notice did not yet include CVE identifiers or CVSS scores. N-central is used by managed service providers (MSPs) and enterprise IT teams to administer endpoints and infrastructure. Compromise of an RMM server can put downstream managed environments at risk. N-central has previously been targeted through separate vulnerabilities, including an authentication bypass covered by Rapid7 in August 2026 . Given the platform's administrative reach and the availability of public exploit code, Rapid7 recommends treating the current disclosure as an emergency. Update #1: On November 10, 2026, N-able released N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2 (build 2026.4.1.26 ), addressing seven CVEs. The vendor plans a follow-up hotfix with further security updates. On November 11, N-able confirmed that hosted N-central servers across all regions had been successfully upgraded. Mitigation guidance Rapid7 strongly recommends that organizations operating on-premises N-central servers upgrade to N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2 (build 2026.4.1.26 ) on an emergency basis outside of normal patching cycles, and keep servers offline until successfully upgraded. Hosted servers are upgraded by N-able. Customers in both hosted and on-premises environments must also upgrade their Agents and Probes. To maintain communication, upgrade Agents first, then Probes, following the vendor's compatibility guidance for the Patch Management Engine (PME). Affected versions: The researcher reports testing N-central Appliance 2026.4.0.31 . N-able's current notice does not specify the full affected-version range. Fixed versions: N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2 (build 2026.4.1.26 ) addresses the seven CVEs listed below. According to N-able's release notes , the hotfix addresses: CVE Description CVE-2026-125883 Multiple XXE vulnerabilities CVE-2026-125878 Multiple OGNL injection vulnerabilities CVE-2026-125879 Local privilege escalation to root through nable -writable syslog-ng configuration CVE-2026-125880 Stored XSS through MMS3 patch metadata in an administrator context CVE-2026-125881 Schema-hint SSRF through service-import schema validation CVE-2026-125882 RCE through file-repository upload path traversal; credited to Nate Fair, Sprocket Security CVE-2026-91000 Local privilege escalation through insecure IPC channels Further security updates are planned in a follow-up hotfix. Organizations should monitor the vendor's guidance and apply subsequent fixes as they become available. Rapid7 also recommends reviewing N-central servers and downstream managed systems for signs of compromise and engaging incident responders if suspicious activity is identified. For the latest mitigation guidance, please refer to N-able's security incident notice . Updates November 10, 2026 : Initial publication. November 11, 2026 : Added hotfix availability, seven CVE identifiers, hosted upgrade confirmation, and updated remediation guidance. Noted the planned follow-up hotfix.

hottest.summary: CISA has added six new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2026-20320 Cisco BroadWorks Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference Vulnerability CVE-2026-111560 Barracuda Networks Multiple Products OS Command Injection Vulnerability CVE-2026-111793 Openwave Messaging Limited Webtop Media Transcoder Incorrect Resource Transfer Between Spheres Vulnerability CVE-2026-116606 Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG) Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel Vulnerability CVE-2026-124194 Microsoft Office Outlook Missing User Interaction for Potentially Unsafe Action Vulnerability CVE-2026-125350 Google Chromium Use-After-Free Vulnerability These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria . Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form . Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.
